astrophysics_verdict.thresholds: Defensible and conservative. 2,000 AU: El-Badry, Rix & Heintz 2021 go to 1 pc (206,000 AU) and, inside 100 pc, keep high-purity pairs to about 10^4 AU, so the cap drops roughly the widest 15-25% of recoverable Gaia pairs (dN/ds ~ s^-1.6 beyond a few hundred AU); within 33 pc the 60 arcsec cap binds first (600 AU at 10 pc, 300 AU at 5 pc), so for the map the effective limit is angular: epsilon Ind A-B (402 arcsec, 1,460 AU) and 40 Eri A-BC (83 arcsec) stay outside, harmlessly since their parallaxes already agree. Pure 3 sigma does reject the motivating pairs: from the fixture lines Luyten 726-8 A 369.93 +- 0.27 (DR2) vs B 373.84 +- 0.56 is 6.3 sigma and Wolf 424 A 231.12 +- 0.58 vs B 223.51 +- 0.53 is 9.7 sigma, because the formal 5-parameter errors on 1-3 arcsec pairs with 16-27 yr orbits ignore orbital motion; 5% admits them (1.1%, 3.3%). The 20% hard cap is necessary: a ground-based sigma of 6.6 mas on 34 mas (CNS5:252) makes 3 sigma a 58% window. The 0.2|mu_p| floor is looser than El-Badry's orbital bound + 2 sigma_mu and dominates for most GCNS pairs; it costs nothing measurable in chance pairs (below) and is what admits pairs whose Hipparcos motion is a photocentre motion.
astrophysics_verdict.chance_alignment: The design's ~15 per sky in GCNS is a safe upper figure but its method is not reproducible: the spike is untracked and 'sky rotated 0.5-2 deg' does not say what was rotated against what (rotating the whole sky breaks no pair). Independent estimate (scratchpad spike on the oracle's parser): rotate a CRC-selected half of all 332,017 stars in RA by 0.7 deg and by 1.9 deg, count pairs whose members lie in different halves (pure chance alignments, x2 for the whole sky). Result: 0 cross-half pairs at both angles (validated: a 7 arcsec rotation yields 10,357 cross-half pairs, half of the real pairs wider than 7 arcsec, as expected), i.e. fewer than about 6 chance pairs per sky at 95%. Order-of-magnitude check agrees: ~250 random neighbours inside the AU-limited radius at 100 pc, times ~0.1 for parallax within 5%, times ~0.05-0.1 for the proper-motion vector, gives 1-3.
astrophysics_verdict.root_vs_weighted_mean: Sound for the class that motivated the rule (a bright Hipparcos/ground primary with a close Gaia companion whose solution the glare and the orbit corrupt: Sirius, alpha Cen, Luyten 726-8, Wolf 424), where a weighted mean would be dominated by the corrupted, formally precise companion value and would move the golden targets. Overstated as a general claim: over the 20,468 non-HIP links the root's parallax error exceeds the companion's in 4,395 (21%), by more than 3x in 1,009, by more than 10x in 238; in 113 links the companion is handed a value more than 5% from its own, more precise one. Example: CNS5:3950 (GJ 12312 A, HIP 78734, Hipparcos 43.67 +- 2.14) drags two clean Gaia companions at 40.68 +- 0.07 and 40.84 +- 0.20 (which agree with each other to 0.4%) from 80.0 to 74.7 ly. Keeping primaries fixed is a defensible engineering choice under the ruling; the note should state the trade-off with these counts. Follow-up to consider: for wide (> 2 arcsec) pairs whose members all have clean Gaia solutions (sigma < 0.1 mas), take the precision-weighted system parallax and move the root too; Sirius and alpha Cen have Hipparcos roots and would be untouched.
astrophysics_verdict.largest_movers_spot_check: Real physical pairs confirmed from the catalogue rows and known systems: beta1/beta2 Tuc (HIP 2487 -> Gaia 4900927434176620160, 26.9 arcsec, 19.36 -> 22.84 mas), kappa1/kappa2 Boo (HIP 69481 -> Gaia 1511793067598402944, 13.5 arcsec), beta1/beta2 Sco (HIP 78821 -> HIP 78820, 13.6 arcsec, 8.19 -> 8.07 mas), GJ 12312 A + two Gaia components (CNS5:3950, flagged a triple in CNS5), Sirius, alpha Cen, Luyten 726-8, Wolf 424, GJ 667 C. Not pairs: the PR's CNS5:252 (95.9 -> 109.4 ly) is GJ 10136 itself, a CNS5 row with no Gaia id (34.0 +- 6.6 mas, Kirkpatrick+2021) sitting 0.024 arcsec from Gaia 2371519626175864960 (29.81 +- 1.26, same proper motion); likewise CNS5:5630 (65.2 -> 75.7 ly, 0.004 arcsec, 50.0 +- 3.0 -> 43.09 +- 1.81), CNS5:3192, CNS5:528 and 12 more of the 15 sub-0.2-arcsec links; and HIP 27890 (HD 40409, V 4.65) 1.03 arcsec from Gaia 4756622820871136640 (G 4.34, plx 36.60 vs 36.67) is the same star, missed by rule (a)'s 1 arcsec GCNS match because its Hipparcos and Gaia proper motions differ by 36 mas/yr.

findings.issue: In the medium and large tiers the companion is moved to the ROOT'S CNS5 parallax, but the root's own row in those tiers comes from gcns.csv (EDR3). Where CNS5 adopted a different value (488 roots, mostly DR2 citations such as Luyten 726-8 A 369.93 vs EDR3 367.712), the pair stays split: 504 of 3,371 medium companions, residuals up to 0.57 ly (Gaia 5849837820492182272 at 54 ly: 54.044 vs root row 53.474); Luyten 726-8 B, a pinned pair, is still 0.053 ly from A in the medium tier. The design's 'in every tier' holds for quick and the map only.
findings.suggestion: In gcnsMain also pin each ROOT row to the table's root_plx when its own value differs (roots are enumerable from the table), or carry the GCNS value of the root in the table for the GCNS tiers. Add a medium-tier check to companions_test or catalogue-verify: for every link whose root is also a tier row, |dist(companion) - dist(root)| below float32 resolution.

findings.issue: 'The root ... normally the best measured' is not quantified. 21% of links (4,395 / 20,468) give the companion a less precise parallax than its own; 113 move it more than 5% away from a value more than 3x more precise (CNS5:3950 / GJ 12312 A: Hipparcos 43.67 +- 2.14 drags two Gaia components at 40.68 +- 0.07 and 40.84 +- 0.20 from 80.0 to 74.7 ly).
findings.suggestion: State the trade-off and the counts in the note; record as a follow-up a precision-weighted system parallax for wide pairs with clean Gaia members (would not touch Sirius or alpha Cen).

findings.file: sim/tools/companions.ail:118-121 (candidates), design note 'Counts' and PR text
findings.issue: 15 links have sep < 0.2 arcsec: CNS5 rows without a Gaia id (CNS5 adopted a non-Gaia parallax: Kirkpatrick+2021, Bartlett+2020, Dieterich+2017) sitting on the GCNS source they are. The rule treats them as binaries and overrides CNS5's curated choice (CNS5:252 34.0 +- 6.6 -> 29.81 +- 1.26; CNS5:5630 50.0 +- 3.0 -> 43.09 +- 1.81). The PR's headline mover CNS5:252 (95.9 -> 109.4 ly) is this case, not a pair. HIP 27890 (HD 40409) 1.03 arcsec from its own Gaia row is the same thing surfaced by rule (a)'s 1 arcsec GCNS match.
findings.suggestion: Classify sub-0.2-arcsec links with matching proper motion as 'same source' in the table (a column or a separate count), and decide explicitly whether to adopt Gaia there; widen rule (a)'s GCNS match to allow for proper-motion differences (2-3 arcsec with |G - V| < 2).

findings.issue: The chance-alignment estimate (~15 per sky in GCNS) and the shape exploration come from an untracked Python spike and the method ('sky rotated 0.5-2 deg') is ambiguous; the independent half-sky rotation gives 0 cross-half pairs at 0.7 and 1.9 deg (< ~6 per sky).
findings.suggestion: Put the estimate in-tree as part of check_companions.py (oracle) or an AILANG entry, with the rotation method stated.

findings.issue: Committed input log carries target index 8 for CNS5:1676; in the shipped stars.json index 8 is now Sirius B. Goldens still match because the sim only echoes the index.

Bright rows rank by Hipparcos V, CNS5/GCNS rows by Gaia G; V - G is +0.3 to +1.5 for K/M stars, so a HIP primary can be out-ranked by a redder Gaia star up to about a magnitude fainter in V. None of the 5 bright links is wrong (beta1 Tuc G 4.33 vs beta2 V 4.53 etc.), so cosmetic today.
findings.suggestion: Convert V to an approximate G (or compare in the same band from hip_main's B-V) before ranking, or document the mixed scale.

notes: PASS at 89/100. The rule is correctly implemented, pure, deterministic, oracle-checked (0 disagreements on 20,468 rows) and mutation-hard (44/44 effective kills). The one substantive defect is finding 1: the medium/large tiers move companions to a CNS5 parallax their primary does not sit at in that tier, so 'every tier' is only true for quick and the map; it should be fixed before the medium tier is relied on for binaries, but it is not a regression (those pairs were split before by their own parallaxes) and does not block merge. Findings 2-4 are honesty-of-the-note items: the precision inversion count, the self-pairs, and the irreproducible chance figure.
